identificationModule.briefTitle: Perfusion Index for Predicting Brachial Plexus Block Success Under General Anesthesia
identificationModule.officialTitle: Usefulness of Pulse Oximeter Perfusion Index for Predicting the Success of Interscalene Brachial Plexus Blockade Under General Anesthesia

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This study was designed to determine whether the success or failure of interscalene brachial plexus block under general anesthesia can be predicted using perfusion index (PI).
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
The success of peripheral nerve blocks is usually evaluated by assessment of sensory and motor function; however, this method cannot be applied in the patient who has uncheckable mental status, e.g. general anesthesia, or who is uncommunicable, e.g. different language user.

The perfusion index (PI) is a numerical value for the ratio between pulsatile and non-pulsatile blood flow measured by a special pulse oximeter, and PI had been proved as a useful tool for evaluation of successful supraclavicular nerve block in awake patients as an objective method.

With the use of ultrasound guidance in skilled hands, it is a reasonable option to perform neuraxial and peripheral regional blocks in sedated or anesthetized patients. However, there has been no evidence of applying PI for predicting the success of nerve block in general anesthetized patients.

armGroups.label: BPB success
armGroups.description: The study included patients aged between 20 and 70 yr who are to undergo elective shoulder surgery under general anesthesia. Patients undergo general anesthesia induction before the interscalene block is performed. Ultrasound-guided interscalene brachial plexus block will be performed in anesthetized patients before surgery. PI monitor will be applied to both blocked and non-blocked limbs using two separate oximeters. And the SUCCESS (or failure) of the block will be confirmed by (1) 30% change of heart rate and blood pressure after incision during operation, and (2) pain score, motor and sensory function test after surgery in the post-anesthesia recovery unit.

interventions.name: Interscalene brachial plexus blocks with ultrasound guidance under general anesthesia
interventions.description: Ultrasound-guidance, interscalene brachial plexus blocks, in-plane technique, perineural injection, 0.5% ropivacaine 12.5ml and 0.2% lidocaine 12.5ml

primaryOutcomes.description: perfusion index measured applied to both blocked and non-blocked limbs using two separate oximeters
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: change between before and 15 minutes after brachial plexus block

secondaryOutcomes.description: heart rate in bpm during operation
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: change between before and 5 minutes after incision of surgical procedure

secondaryOutcomes.description: blood pressure in mmHg during operation
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: change between before and 5 minutes after incision of surgical procedure

secondaryOutcomes.description: Numeric rating scale for pain on a 0-10 scale where 0=no pain and 10=unbearable pain

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Sensory function test on supraclavicular nerve and axillary nerve
secondaryOutcomes.description: 0-2 scale where 0=no block; 1=analgesia (patient can feel touch, not cold); 2=anesthesia (patient cannot feel touch)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Motor function test on supraclavicular nerve and axillary nerve and
secondaryOutcomes.description: 0-2 scale where 0 = no block; 1 = paresis; 2 = paralysis

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 20-70 years old,
* BMI 20-35 kg.m-2,
* elective shoulder surgery,
* ASA physical status I-III

Exclusion Criteria:

* refusal of the patient,
* comorbid with serious vascular disease,
* diabetes,
* allergy to local anesthetics,
* patients on regular opioids,
* peripheral neuropathy.
eligibilityModule.studyPopulation: patients aged 20-70 who are scheduled for shoulder surgery under general anesthesia, with ASA physical status I-III
